summary: @servicetitan/cp-react-hooks preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes obfuscated bundled payload
details: The package advertises itself as a React hooks library but ships an obfuscated `setup.mjs` as its `preinstall` script. On `npm install`, `setup.mjs` downloads the Bun JavaScript runtime from https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/<arch>.zip, extracts it to a temp directory, chmods it executable, and then invokes it via `execFileSync` to run a sibling file `math_init.js`. `math_init.js` is a ~727KB Bun-compiled bundle (`// @bun @bun-cjs`) with obfuscator.io-style string-array rotation, char-code array decoding, and control-flow flattening; its filename does not match its contents and it is not a math library. The preinstall entrypoint itself is obfuscated with `_0x`-style identifiers and object-literal dispatch tables that hide the strings `"bun"`, the download URL, `execFileSync`, and the target path. A React hooks library has no need for a second JavaScript runtime fetched at install time solely to execute an opaque bundled blob outside Node's normal inspection path; the delivery chain (obfuscated lifecycle script + fetch of an alternate runtime + execution of an obfuscated sibling bundle via that runtime) is a supply-chain dropper pattern that fires automatically on default install.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
